metadata.title: Canadian Arctic trade and logistics corridors
metadata.geometry_method: Hand-placed schematic waypoints; broad corridor geography only. Not AIS tracks or official navigation guidance.
metadata.time_relationship: Route visibility is independent of the ice-map year and season. Showing a corridor does not certify access in the selected year.
metadata.scope: Canada and the Northwest Passage. Grays Bay market connectors are inferred concepts, not approved services.

properties.name: Northwest Passage · Victoria Strait
properties.summary: Southern passage variant (3A) through the Canadian archipelago. Recorded NWP transits do not establish a regular container service on this specific line.
properties.cargo: Bulk and general cargo have transited the NWP; this corridor is not a carrier timetable.
properties.season: Access varies by vessel and year; no fixed opening date.
constraints: Shallow coastal reaches and narrow channels.
Ice can remain in choke points even when regional mean concentration falls.
Individual vessel suitability requires separate assessment.

properties.name: Northwest Passage · Prince of Wales
properties.summary: Northern passage variant (1) using Viscount Melville Sound and Prince of Wales Strait. A mapped corridor, not a year-round trade lane.
properties.season: Ice conditions may prevent a complete transit in a given season.
constraints: Multi-year ice can affect northern channels.
Narrow strait and limited support infrastructure.

properties.name: Northwest Passage · Rae / Simpson
properties.summary: Southern variant (3B) east and south of King William Island, near Gjoa Haven.
constraints: Shoals, narrow channels and draft restrictions.
Not interchangeable with deeper passage variants.

properties.name: Québec → Baffin / Kitikmeot sealift
properties.summary: NEAS lists Pond Inlet, Resolute Bay, Cambridge Bay, Gjoa Haven and other Arctic communities as service areas. This line illustrates the sea connection, not a published voyage itinerary.
properties.cargo: Community supplies, equipment and project freight.
properties.season: Seasonal sealift; sailing calls and order vary by operator and year.
constraints: Local unloading facilities and vessel draft.
Ice-dependent sailing schedules; not every voyage follows every stop shown.

properties.name: Tuktoyaktuk → western Arctic resupply
properties.summary: MTS supplies Western Arctic communities with deck cargo and petroleum. The coastal sketch connects Tuktoyaktuk, Paulatuk and Kugluktuk; it omits individual delivery calls.
properties.season: Annual scheduled service; consult the current sailing schedule.
constraints: Weather, ice and unloading access.
Do not infer a current MTS Cambridge Bay service from this line.

properties.name: Churchill → Atlantic / Europe
properties.summary: Churchill announced a Europe-bound grain loading in August 2026. The port links Canadian inland freight with international markets; the European endpoint here is only a gateway.
properties.cargo: Grain and other bulk exports; northern resupply.
properties.season: Current corridor is shown as seasonal, without assuming year-round operation.
constraints: Rail and port handling capacity.
Ice and voyage schedules; this is not a Northwest Passage crossing.

properties.name: Grays Bay → Pacific connection
properties.summary: Potential feeder from the proposed port to the western NWP and Bering Strait. This is our logistics concept, not an announced Asia shipping service.
properties.cargo: Potential mineral exports and inbound project / community supplies.
properties.season: No opening year assigned; depends on the port project and voyage conditions.
constraints: Port approval, construction and cargo commitments.
Shallow coastal passages may constrain bulk-vessel draft.
Distance alone does not establish commercial viability.

properties.name: Grays Bay ↔ Jericho road
properties.summary: The project proposes an approximately 230 km all-season road to Jericho Station. This straight line joins the published endpoints; it is not the surveyed road alignment.
properties.cargo: Land–sea transfer of mineral and supply freight.
properties.season: Proposed all-season road; the associated marine operation remains ice dependent.
constraints: Environmental review, financing and construction.
Existing winter-road linkage does not equal a completed all-season route to southern Canada.
